thesis.company_overview:
Tenet Healthcare Corporation (NYSE: THC) is a Dallas-headquartered diversified healthcare services company that sells clinical capacity and the administrative infrastructure behind it: acute-care and specialty hospital operations, a large ambulatory surgery centre platform, and healthcare-services capabilities spanning revenue-cycle management and value-based care. Demand is driven by patient volumes and acuity mix, commercial and government payer rates, and the multi-year migration of procedures from inpatient to ambulatory settings. On a trailing-twelve-month basis the group generated $21.81B of revenue and $5.31B of EBITDA at an 82.8% gross margin and a 19.5% operating margin. A segment revenue breakdown was not available for this issuer; see the latest annual report for business-line detail. Geographic revenue breakdown was likewise not available for this issuer, so no regional mix is asserted here.

The durable moat is structural rather than technological. Hospital and ambulatory surgery capacity in demographically attractive markets is licence- and certificate-of-need constrained, physician alignment and employed-provider networks create referral lock-in, and scale in payer contracting and group purchasing lowers unit cost — the operating margin progression from 16.1% (FY2025, annual basis) to 19.5% (TTM) evidences that leverage. The offsetting structural features are capital intensity (capex of 4.5% of revenue, trailing twelve months) and pricing that is re-set annually through negotiation with concentrated commercial payers and administered government programmes, so the moat protects share of a market whose economics are repriced rather than guaranteed. Enterprise value bridges across $11.08B of net debt and $4.04B of noncontrolling interest.
thesis.competitor_analysis: Industry economics for THC are set by capital intensity, administered and negotiated reimbursement, local-market density and certificate/licence constraints rather than by differentiated product IP — advantages are scale in payer contracting, physician alignment and ambulatory footprint, not proprietary technology. A peer screen did not run for this ticker in this run: the peer-financials fetch returned no usable comp set, so no peer multiples are cited here and no peer-relative premium or discount is asserted. The only multiple evidence available is the issuer's own tape — TTM EV/EBITDA of roughly 7.0× against a five-year median of 6.2× (p25 3.91×, p75 6.72×), an own-history classification of expensive. Positioning is therefore summarized qualitatively: durable advantages are licence-constrained capacity and contracting scale, while any claim of relative cheapness or richness versus peers would be unsupported by the data on hand.

thesis.narrative:
We initiate on Tenet Healthcare with a HOLD. At the authoritative $271.60 market price the stock sits inside a published valuation band of $212.91–$541.80, the span of the two surviving method mids — DCF at $541.80 (own range $433.44–$650.16, weight 0.85) and EV/EBITDA at $212.91 (own range $120.36–$305.46, weight 0.72). That 2.5× method spread, inside a medium-confidence blend, is precisely why we publish a range and a directional verdict rather than a point estimate: there is no single corroborated fair value here, and the market price is fairly valued within the band rather than at either extreme.

The operating record supports neither an aggressive long nor a short. On a trailing-twelve-month basis the franchise produced $21.81B of revenue, $5.31B of EBITDA, an 82.8% gross margin and a 19.5% operating margin, with the operating margin up from 16.1% on the FY2025 annual basis. The balance sheet is not the binding constraint either: the Merton/KMV model yields a 3.52 distance to default, a 1-year default probability of 0.02% and 37.7% market leverage. Earnings-based value looks undemanding at a P/E of 9.76× on TTM net income attributable to the parent, which is the counterweight to the expensive own-history multiple read.

Where the market stands versus the model is the crux. Held to the model's growth fade, the $271.60 price solves to a 10.3% implied WACC; holding the 7.45% WACC fixed, the price solves to -2.6%/yr revenue growth held flat across the 10-year horizon — against the model's own fade of 3.6% in FY1 declining to 3.0% in FY10, a 3.3%/yr average. Those are different constructs, and the market's flat negative solve is a conservative, not a demanding, read of the cash flows. What tempers the upside is positioning: the shares are +42.9% over the trailing year, 91% of the way up the 52-week range and only -4.0% off the high, while insiders were net sellers to the tune of -$49,991,274 over 90 days with $0 of open-market purchases. Momentum and flow argue for patience, not accumulation — HOLD.

Price action, not news flow, is carrying the narrative: +42.9% over the trailing year with the shares at 91% of their 52-week range and only -4.0% below the high. That combination supports a HOLD — the tape is constructive, but -$49,991,274 of 90-day insider net selling against $0 of open-market purchases argues against chasing the move.

thesis.valuation_overview:
Two methods survived into the published blend, and they disagree by 2.5× — the reason the target is a range, not a point. The DCF anchors the top at a mid of $541.80 (own range $433.44–$650.16, weight 0.85) because it capitalizes ten years of modelled free cash flow at a 7.45% WACC and a 3.0% perpetuity growth rate applied after the explicit window. The EV/EBITDA read lands at a mid of $212.91 (own range $120.36–$305.46, weight 0.72) because it applies the issuer's own five-year multiple band (median 6.2×, p25 3.91×, p75 6.72×) to TTM EBITDA of $5.31B, then bridges to equity across $11.08B of net debt and $4.04B of noncontrolling interest.

The gap is a cash-flow-versus-multiple argument: the DCF pays for a declining growth fade averaging 3.3%/yr (3.6% FY1 to 3.0% FY10), while the multiple framework refuses to pay for it against a multiple the issuer's own history labels expensive at ~7.0× versus a 6.2× median. Because the $271.60 market price falls inside the resulting $212.91–$541.80 band, the methods collectively say fairly valued, and the 2.5× span exceeds the 2× corroboration limit, so we publish the range and the HOLD rather than invent a point inside it.
